unknown_model.title: Model not checked yet
unknown_model.description:
The {model} has not been checked with this integration yet. Its entities are built from what it reports, but some settings may be missing or read wrongly.

The capability check asks the receiver about 150 read-only questions (nothing is changed) once it is connected, and puts the answers into the diagnostics file. You can then attach that file to a prefilled issue on GitHub, so the model can be supported properly. Nothing is sent anywhere by itself.

check.title: Check capabilities
check.description: Asks the receiver about 150 read-only questions over the existing connection; nothing is changed. It takes up to a minute and a half; commands from Home Assistant still go first. The answers go into the diagnostics file.

check_done.title: Check finished
check_done.description:
The {model} answered {answered} of {total} questions. The answers are in the diagnostics file (Settings → Devices & services → Denon AVR Plus → ⋮ → Download diagnostics).

To help support this model, open [this prefilled issue on GitHub]({url}) and attach the diagnostics file. Read the file before you attach it; addresses are already replaced.

telnet_unavailable.title: {model} does not accept a control connection
telnet_unavailable.description:
The {model} answers on the network, but has not accepted a telnet connection on port 23 for several minutes. Until it does, the media players work over the web interface only: power, volume, mute and source, with up to 10 seconds delay. All other settings are unavailable.

The receiver allows only one telnet connection at a time. Common causes:

- Another integration or program holds that connection, for example the official Denon AVR integration or another home automation system. Remove or disable it for this receiver.
- A firewall or VLAN rule blocks port 23 between Home Assistant and the receiver, while the web ports are open.

The message disappears by itself as soon as the connection works again.

heos_playback_error.title: {model} could not play it
heos_playback_error.description:
HEOS on the {model} reported a playback error: {error}

Common causes are an address the receiver cannot reach, a format it does not play, or a service that needs a sign-in in the HEOS app. The message disappears by itself as soon as something plays again.

send_command.name: Send command
send_command.description: Sends a raw telnet command to the receiver, for settings without an entity. Asked for a response, returns the receiver's replies.

command.name: Command
command.description: As in the protocol documents, for example PSDYNEQ ON or MV?. Printable ASCII, at most {max_length} characters.

store_tuner_preset.name: Store tuner preset
store_tuner_preset.description: Stores the station the tuner plays as a preset of the receiver. The tuner must be the source of a zone that is on.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: 1 to 56 (on older receivers A1 to G8, counted the same way).

snapshot.name: Snapshot
snapshot.description: Keeps what the zone does now: power, input, volume and mute. The sound mode follows the input.

restore.name: Restore
restore.description: Puts the zone back as the last snapshot found it.

get_queue.description: The HEOS queue of the receiver: queue id, title, artist, album and image of each item (the first 100).

remove_from_queue.name: Remove from queue

queue_ids.name: Queue ids

move_queue_item.name: Move queue items
move_queue_item.description: Moves items of the HEOS queue to another place.

queue_ids.name: Queue ids
queue_ids.description: The queue ids of the items, as get_queue lists them.

destination.description: The place to move them to, counted from 1.
